records.description: The reviewed KamLAND reactor disappearance, SNO active-flavor transformation, Super-Kamiokande atmospheric disappearance and OPERA accelerator tau-appearance results support flavor change compatible with their declared oscillation models across different preparations and responses. Their counts, fluxes, averaged probabilities and conditional fit parameters are distinct observables. This synthesis preserves those boundaries and supplies neither a pooled transition probability nor a new global fit.
records.name: Neutrino oscillation evidence across preparations
openObligations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. records.description: With the usual fermion content, one Higgs doublet and no right-handed neutrino singlets, the minimal renormalizable Standard Model has no neutrino Dirac Yukawa term and leaves neutrinos massless. Formal extensions can add singlet neutrinos and Dirac masses, with total lepton number imposed to exclude Majorana terms, or allow lepton-number-violating Majorana masses. A dimension-five operator built from the lepton and Higgs doublets can instead generate a Majorana mass after electroweak symmetry breaking. These are alternative model constructions; flavor-oscillation evidence alone does not select one.
records.name: Neutrino mass-model boundary
openObligations: The massless statement uses the minimal renormalizable field content and its accidental symmetries. It is not a prohibition on all gauge-invariant Standard Model effective operators: the stated dimension-five extension changes that assumption.

Dirac and Majorana alternatives require different field or symmetry assumptions. A see-saw construction additionally needs a hierarchy and matching assumptions; no such hierarchy, heavy state, Yukawa coefficient or new-physics scale is inferred here.

Nonzero oscillation mass-squared differences do not determine all absolute masses, prove that all three masses are positive, identify a Dirac/Majorana assignment, or establish the charged-fermion mass route for neutrinos. Direct kinematic, cosmological and lepton-number-violating searches retain separate inference contexts.

records.name: Coherent neutrino propagation in matter
openObligations: Use a closed unitary three-active-neutrino model with standard weak interactions, hbar=c=1 and fixed positive energy in the ultrarelativistic coherent forward-scattering approximation. The prescribed medium is electrically neutral, unpolarized and locally isotropic, with nonrelativistic electrons, protons and neutrons and no appreciable muon/tau population. Incoherent scattering, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require different models.

The vector f contains flavor amplitudes, with the already declared U_alpha,i convention. The review writes its basic evolution equation in the vacuum mass basis; multiplication by the constant U gives the stated flavor-basis Hamiltonian. For antineutrinos both U becomes U* and the charged-current potential changes sign. A merely diagonal potential cannot in general be discarded; the neutral-current term is removable here because it is common to all three active flavors.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. This model does not determine absolute mass, Dirac/Majorana nature, an origin mechanism, universal carrier minima or a temporal emergence order.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.

records.description: In a supplied closed unitary three-active-neutrino model, define U=R23 R13(delta) R12 P. Each real ij rotation acts on its plane with block [[cij,sij],[-sij,cij]] and as identity on the remaining direction, with cij=cos(thetaij) and sij=sin(thetaij); the 1-3 block is [[c13,s13 exp(-i delta)],[-s13 exp(i delta),c13]]. For generic three-mass mixing, charged-lepton and Dirac-neutrino rephasings leave three angles and one Dirac phase, with P=I. In the Majorana alternative use P=diag(exp(i eta1),exp(i eta2),1); these two extra column phases cancel from ordinary mass-induced flavor-oscillation probabilities.
records.name: Three-active-neutrino mixing parameterization
openObligations: The supplied 3-by-3 unitary model is distinct from a general 3-by-n charged-current matrix or an effective light-sector submatrix after heavy states are removed. The latter need not be exactly unitary; this definition does not establish that extra states are absent.

The phase count assumes generic nondegenerate nonzero masses. Degenerate masses, a massless state or vanishing mixing angles can remove phases or their observable effects. A nontrivial mixing matrix need not violate CP, and a complex entry alone is not a rephasing-invariant measurement.

For the same ordinary vacuum channel, U_prime(alpha,i)=exp(i r_alpha) U(alpha,i) exp(i c_i) gives A_prime(alpha,beta)=exp(i(r_beta-r_alpha)) A(alpha,beta), so its probability is unchanged. This column-phase invariance of the oscillation amplitude does not permit arbitrary rephasing of a Majorana field at fixed real mass in the full Lagrangian.

Majorana column-phase cancellation concerns ordinary lepton-number-conserving oscillations. It does not make those phases unphysical in all processes or identify neutrinos as Dirac or Majorana. The chosen angles, phases and conventions supply no fitted parameter values or current ordering preference.

A degenerate pair, unmixed channel or suppressed interference need not show an oscillatory signal.

A single vacuum mass eigenstate acquires only a phase in its internal state; its flavor-readout probabilities |U_alpha,i|^2 do not oscillate. An incoherent density matrix diagonal in the vacuum mass basis also has constant vacuum flavor probabilities. These are not statements that vacuum mass states remain instantaneous eigenstates in arbitrary varying matter, or that packet position is stationary.

No causal maintenance or downward constraint is inferred from these definition dependencies.

Within this oscillation model, mass-squared differences constrain differences only. They do not determine the absolute mass scale, require every individual mass to be nonzero, select Dirac versus Majorana character or supply a unique mass-generation extension. Mass origin remains a separate scope.

Continuous weak scattering or repeated projective collapse is not the coherent phase mechanism. A specified source, medium and detector determine which probability or weighted response is appropriate; transport and cosmological claims need additional inputs.

limitations: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

The SOF signal is a classical cyclotron amplitude produced by two separated pulses, not a quantum-state amplitude or an entanglement measurement. Figure 1 uses evolution times up to 50 s for the precision estimate.

Figure 2 compares an N+ ion at approximately 5 V with the same species at 10 V and an N2+ ion at 10 V, with a 22.5 mV axial offset. The approximately 3 ppb unequal-voltage shift disappears at the reported precision with the common-voltage procedure.

Table I bounds residual magnetic, electrostatic and relativistic systematic terms at approximately 0.030, 0.025 and 0.020 ppb for the specified N+/N2+ settings. These are configuration-specific error estimates, not zero corrections or universal bounds.

The first two Table II(a) reference ratios depend on electron mass and binding energies. Their agreement near 0.15 ppb tests those controls; it does not prove absence of every systematic effect in all other ion comparisons.
The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

For the same magnetic field, omega_2/omega_1=(m_1/abs(q_1))/(m_2/abs(q_2)). Equal charges permit a mass ratio; the Ar+/Ar++ entry requires the charge factor and is not a literal ratio of almost equal ionic masses.
The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

A charged-ion frequency, neutral-atom mass and inferred neutron mass are different quantities. These results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal constituent minimum.
